scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc2 default route / gateway configuration
Mechanism: pc2's default route (via 200.1.1.1) has been deleted,
  leaving only the connected 200.1.1.0/24 route. Any packet to an
  off-subnet destination fails immediately in pc2's own kernel
  with ENETUNREACH ("Network is unreachable") -- nothing is even
  transmitted, which is why the error is instant rather than a
  timeout. On-subnet traffic to 200.1.1.1 still works. The network
  side is fully healthy: router2 still advertises 200.1.1.0/24,
  the eBGP session is Established, and pc1's pings ARE delivered
  to pc2 -- but pc2 has no route for the replies, so pc1 sees
  timeouts.
Localization: pc2
Root cause: missing default route on pc2 (no gateway configured)
Fix: `ip route add default via 200.1.1.1 dev eth0` on pc2
scenario.fix_spec:
Restore pc2's default route -- `ip route add default via 200.1.1.1 dev eth0`
on pc2. Off-subnet connectivity returns immediately; no router or BGP change
is needed.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is entirely on pc2 — its kernel routing table is missing a
default gateway. pc2 only has the auto-generated connected route
200.1.1.0/24 dev eth0 (its own LAN). There is no default route and no
specific route to the pc1 subnet (195.11.14.0/24). When an application
on pc2 tries to reach any address outside 200.1.1.0/24, the kernel
performs a route lookup, finds no match, and immediately returns
ENETUNREACH to the socket — producing the "Network is unreachable"
error without even sending a packet. This is why the failure is
instantaneous rather than a timeout.

The asymmetric symptom on pc1 (timeouts rather than immediate failure)
confirms the diagnosis: pc1 has a valid default route (via 195.11.14.1
→ router1), both routers have a fully converged BGP session exchanging
each other's LAN prefix (router1 knows 200.1.1.0/24 via BGP from
router2, and vice-versa for 195.11.14.0/24), so ICMP echo-requests
from pc1 do reach pc2 successfully. However, pc2's reply packets to
195.11.14.2 find no route and are silently discarded, causing pc1 to
see timeouts.

Root cause: the default route on pc2 was removed during maintenance,
leaving it with no path to any off-LAN destination.

Corrective fix: restore the default route on pc2:
  ip route add default via 200.1.1.1
(200.1.1.1 is router2's eth1, pc2's gateway, confirmed up.)
To make it persistent across reboots, add the equivalent entry to the
host's startup configuration or /etc/network/interfaces.
